latest_nl_proof:
Fix h >= 0. Let S_h be the set of pairs (Lambda, x) such that Lambda is a numerical semigroup of genus h and x is an effective generator of Lambda, and let T_{h+1} be the set of numerical semigroups Gamma of genus h+1. Define f : S_h -> T_{h+1} by f(Lambda, x) = Lambda minus {x}. We prove that f is a bijection by constructing an inverse.

First we show that f is well defined. Take (Lambda, x) in S_h and set Gamma = Lambda minus {x}. Because x is effective, x is in particular a positive minimal generator of Lambda and x > F(Lambda).

1. Gamma contains 0, because x is positive.

2. Gamma is cofinite in the nonnegative integers, since its complement is exactly the union of the complement of Lambda with the singleton {x}; this union is disjoint because x belongs to Lambda. Therefore genus(Gamma) = genus(Lambda) + 1 = h + 1.

3. Gamma is closed under addition. Let a and b belong to Gamma. Since Gamma is contained in Lambda and Lambda is additive, a + b belongs to Lambda. The only way a + b could fail to lie in Gamma is if a + b = x, because Gamma was obtained from Lambda by removing only x. So suppose a + b = x. If one of a, b were 0, the other would have to be x, impossible because x is not in Gamma. Hence a and b are both positive. But then x = a + b writes x as a sum of two positive elements of Lambda, contradicting that x is a minimal generator of Lambda. So a + b cannot equal x. Hence a + b belongs to Lambda minus {x} = Gamma.

Thus Gamma is a numerical semigroup of genus h+1, so f is well defined.

We also record a useful fact: F(Gamma) = x. Indeed, x is not in Gamma. On the other hand, if n > x, then n > F(Lambda) because x > F(Lambda), so n belongs to Lambda; and since n is not equal to x, it also belongs to Gamma. Therefore Gamma has no missing element larger than x, while x itself is missing, so F(Gamma) = x.

Now define a map g : T_{h+1} -> S_h as follows. For Gamma in T_{h+1}, set x = F(Gamma) and Lambda = Gamma union {x}. This makes sense because genus(Gamma) = h+1 >= 1, so Gamma is not the whole set of nonnegative integers; hence F(Gamma) is an actual missing nonnegative integer.

We check that (Lambda, x) lies in S_h.

1. Lambda is a numerical semigroup.

- It contains 0 because Gamma does.

- It is cofinite because it is obtained from the cofinite set Gamma by adjoining one element.

- Its genus is h, because its complement is the complement of Gamma with the single gap x removed. Hence genus(Lambda) = genus(Gamma) - 1 = h.

- It is closed under addition. Let a and b belong to Lambda.
  * If both a and b belong to Gamma, then a + b belongs to Gamma, since Gamma is a numerical semigroup.
  * If one summand is x and the other is 0, then the sum is x, which belongs to Lambda.
  * If one summand is x and the other is a positive element of Gamma, then the sum is strictly greater than x = F(Gamma), so it belongs to Gamma, hence to Lambda.
  * If a = b = x, then 2x > x = F(Gamma), so 2x belongs to Gamma, hence to Lambda.
Therefore Lambda is an additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers.

So Lambda is a numerical semigroup of genus h.

2. x is a minimal generator of Lambda. Certainly x belongs to Lambda, and x is positive because 0 belongs to Gamma while x = F(Gamma) does not. Suppose for contradiction that x = a + b with positive a, b in Lambda. Then a < x and b < x, so neither a nor b can equal x. Since Lambda = Gamma union {x}, it follows that a and b both belong to Gamma. Because Gamma is additive, x = a + b would then belong to Gamma, contradicting the definition of x = F(Gamma). Hence no such decomposition exists, so x is a minimal generator of Lambda.

3. x is effective. Since x is not in Gamma but every integer greater than x belongs to Gamma by the definition of Frobenius number, every gap of Lambda is strictly less than x. Therefore F(Lambda) < x. (If Lambda has no gaps, then by convention F(Lambda) = -1, which is still < x.) So x is an effective generator of Lambda.

Finally, by construction, c_x(Lambda) = Lambda minus {x} = Gamma. Hence g is well defined and f(g(Gamma)) = Gamma for every Gamma in T_{h+1}.

For the other composition, take any (Lambda, x) in S_h and set Gamma = f(Lambda, x) = Lambda minus {x}. From the first part we already proved that F(Gamma) = x. Therefore

g(f(Lambda, x)) = g(Gamma) = (Gamma union {F(Gamma)}, F(Gamma)) = ((Lambda minus {x}) union {x}, x) = (Lambda, x).

So g is a two-sided inverse of f. Therefore f is a bijection from S_h onto T_{h+1}.

This also gives the equivalent uniqueness statement. If Gamma is a numerical semigroup of genus h+1 and Gamma = M minus {y} for some numerical semigroup M of genus h and some effective generator y of M, then applying the first part to (M, y) shows that F(Gamma) = y. Hence y is uniquely determined, namely y = F(Gamma), and then M is uniquely determined as Gamma union {F(Gamma)}. So the unique witnesses are exactly Lambda = Gamma union {F(Gamma)} and x = F(Gamma). This is precisely the claimed equivalence.
role_in_parent: Reindexes genus-(h+1) semigroups by genus-h parents and deleted effective generators.
statement_nl: Let h be a nonnegative integer. A numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers containing 0, and its genus is the number of nonnegative integers not belonging to it. For a numerical semigroup Lambda, let F(Lambda) be the largest integer not in Lambda, with the convention F(Lambda) = -1 for the whole set of nonnegative integers. A minimal generator of Lambda is a positive element x of Lambda that cannot be written as a+b with positive a,b in Lambda. An effective generator of Lambda is a minimal generator x satisfying x > F(Lambda). For an effective generator x of Lambda, let c_x(Lambda) be the set obtained from Lambda by removing x. Then the map sending a pair (Lambda, x), where Lambda is a numerical semigroup of genus h and x is an effective generator of Lambda, to c_x(Lambda) is a bijection onto the set of numerical semigroups of genus h+1. Equivalently: if Gamma is a numerical semigroup of genus h+1, then there is a unique pair (Lambda, x) with Lambda a numerical semigroup of genus h and x an effective generator of Lambda such that Gamma = c_x(Lambda); the unique witnesses are Lambda = Gamma union {F(Gamma)} and x = F(Gamma).

domain_restrictions: Numerical semigroup means: Λ ⊆ Z_{≥0}, additive submonoid, 0 ∈ Λ, and Z_{≥0} \ Λ is finite (cofinite submonoid).
genus(Λ) = |Z_{≥0} \ Λ|, so genus(Λ)=h implies exactly h nonnegative integers are missing from Λ.
F(Λ) is defined as the largest integer not in Λ; if Λ = Z_{≥0} (equivalently genus(Λ)=0), then F(Λ)=-1 by convention.
A minimal generator x of Λ is required to be a positive element x ∈ Λ such that x cannot be expressed as a+b with a,b ∈ Λ and a>0, b>0.
x is an effective generator of Λ iff: (i) x is a minimal generator of Λ and (ii) x > F(Λ).
c_x(Λ) is defined as the set obtained from Λ by removing x, i.e. c_x(Λ)=Λ \ {x} (with x ∈ Λ).
In the bijection claim: the mapping domain consists only of pairs (Λ,x) where genus(Λ)=h and x is an effective generator of Λ.
In the equivalent claim: Γ has genus h+1, hence Γ is not the whole set Z_{≥0}, so F(Γ) is not forced to be -1 (and is the unique candidate witness x=F(Γ)).
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every h ∈ Z_{≥0}, the function f defined by f(Λ,x)=c_x(Λ)=Λ\{x}, where Λ ranges over numerical semigroups with genus(Λ)=h and x ranges over the effective generators of Λ, is a bijection onto the set of numerical semigroups Γ with genus(Γ)=h+1. Equivalently: for every numerical semigroup Γ with genus(Γ)=h+1, there exists exactly one pair (Λ,x) such that genus(Λ)=h, x is an effective generator of Λ, and Γ=Λ\{x}; moreover these unique witnesses satisfy Λ = Γ ∪ {F(Γ)} and x = F(Γ).
quantifier_order: ∀ Γ (numerical semigroup with genus(Γ)=h+1) ∃! Λ, ∃! x such that: genus(Λ)=h, x is an effective generator of Λ, and Γ = c_x(Λ)

witness_dependencies: Given Γ with genus(Γ)=h+1, the unique witness semigroup is Λ := Γ ∪ {F(Γ)}.
Given Γ with genus(Γ)=h+1, the unique witness generator is x := F(Γ).
The witness x is required to be an effective generator of the constructed Λ = Γ ∪ {F(Γ)} (i.e. x is a minimal generator of Λ and x > F(Λ)), and the construction ensures Γ = c_x(Λ) = Λ \ {x}.
